summary.name: PostOps: A Non-Surgical Tale of Software, Fragility, and Reliability
summary.one_liner: A 2013 USENIX LISA conference talk by Todd Underwood of Google arguing for moving beyond DevOps-style operations toward "PostOps," which aims to end toil through software.
use_cases: Understanding the case for moving beyond DevOps
Reading background on SRE culture and philosophy
Finding conference material from USENIX LISA 2013
Citing the PostOps talk in reliability discussions
summary.what_it_does: The page is the abstract and speaker bio for a talk presented at USENIX LISA 2013 in Washington, D.C. The talk argues that distributed computing enables DevOps as a collaborative approach to deploying and managing systems, and that the malleability of software should be used to move beyond operations entirely. It presents PostOps as a call to end toil. The speaker, Todd Underwood, is a site reliability manager at Google, and previously worked on operations, security and peering at Renesys and was CTO of an ISP. The page lists citation metadata and notes that USENIX makes papers and post-event slides and video free to access. It does not include the slides, video or a transcript.
